label: cor-derivatives-have-no-removable-or-jump-discontinuities
tail:
VERDICT: DEFECTS

FINDING 1
  location: Statement, second sentence
  severity: nonfatal
  claim: "Any discontinuity of a derivative is therefore essential"
  evidence: The proof (steps 1.1–1.2) only addresses the case where c is a limit point of both A⁻ and A⁺ (an interior point relative to the interval) because removable and jump are defined only in that situation. The statement does not restrict itself to interior points, so a discontinuity at an endpoint—where only one one‑sided limit is defined—is not covered. The definition allows a discontinuity of the first kind at such a point when the one‑sided limit exists, and the proof does not rule that out. Hence the inference that *any* discontinuity is essential is not fully supported by the given steps. (The gap can be closed by a similar intermediate‑value argument on a one‑sided interval, so it is nonfatal.)

BOUNDARY: The proof implicitly treats interior points; the endpoint case is not examined. The same IVP argument, adapted to a one‑sided neighbourhood, quickly shows that a derivative cannot have a first‑kind discontinuity at an endpoint either, so the overall claim remains correct.

SOURCES: thm-darboux-theorem-for-derivatives, def-classification-of-discontinuities, def-one-sided-limits inspected; each cited fact matches its required usage.

CHECKED: Title, public claim, every numbered step, and Remarks verified.
